clue.text: Exceptionally good curiosities left

parts.note: phenomena are remarkable things or wonders, so curiosities

explanation.surface: Someone praises a collection of oddities that were left behind as outstanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Something phenomenal is remarkable or extraordinary, an informal synonym for outstandingly good.

clue.text: What sounds like full agreement

indicators.note: sounds like tells us the entry is said the same as a word for full

parts.note: a full room is packed

explanation.surface: A question about what sounds like total consensus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full agreement' reads as one phrase meaning total consensus, but 'full' is the word heard and 'agreement' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pact is a formal treaty or deal between parties, a kind of agreement.

clue.text: Full of beans in Greece, mad about temperature

indicators.note: about says the scrambled letters go around the abbreviation for temperature
mad suggests the letters of in Greece go wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lively holidaymaker in Greece goes crazy over the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word placing someone in Greece, but it is part of the fodder; 'mad' scrambles it with GREECE to ENERGEIC, and 'about' wraps that round T.
explanation.definitionFit: Full of beans is an idiom for lively and vigorous, which is what energetic means.

clue.text: Where playing card displays pips, seemingly?

definitions.text: Where playing card displays pips, seemingly?

parts.words: Where playing card displays pips, seemingly
parts.note: the pips of a playing card are printed on its front surface; the idiom meaning apparently is read literally as the card's front

explanation.surface: A question about where the suit symbols appear on a playing card.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase meaning 'apparently' is read literally: the pips are on the card's front side, and 'seemingly' supplies the idiom's real sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means judging by appearances, apparently, and literally names the front of a card.

clue.text: Stylish article written after member appears in film

indicators.note: appears in says this pair sits inside the film's title

parts.note: ET is the Spielberg film about an extra-terrestrial

indicators.note: written after places the article following the limb in the sequence

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An item of clothing written about after a body part features in a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means graceful and refined in appearance, a close synonym of stylish.

clue.text: Lecture a daughter over clothes

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first pieces above the next one

parts.note: D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter
to clothe someone is to dress them

explanation.surface: A parent scolds a daughter about what she wears.
explanation.definitionFit: An address is a formal speech, so a lecture; as a verb, to address an audience is to lecture it.

clue.text: Closely examine small container for storing film

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
film reels are kept in metal cans

explanation.surface: Someone inspects a little canister of movie film.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan something is to scrutinise it carefully, looking over every part.

clue.text: Group of singers sing endlessly about love

indicators.note: about says the shortened word goes around the letter for love
endlessly says the word for sing loses its final letter

parts.note: birds chirp, that is, sing
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A vocal group that sings on and on about love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts CHIRP to CHIR, and 'about' wraps it round O.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir is an organised body of singers, as in a church or school.

clue.text: Guys taking care of blossoming business?

definitions.text: Guys taking care of blossoming business?

parts.words: Guys taking care of blossoming business
parts.note: a thriving business is blossoming, but here the blossoms are literal: people who raise plants for sale, and the men who nurse young plants

explanation.surface: Men who look after a firm that is doing well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blossoming' seems to mean prospering; read literally it is about flowers, which these growers tend.
explanation.definitionFit: Nurserymen raise and sell young plants and trees in a plant nursery.

clue.text: Talk about European do

indicators.note: about says the word for talk goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: a chat is an informal talk

explanation.surface: A conversation about what a European might do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do' here is the slang verb meaning swindle, not an ordinary action.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone is slang for swindling them, which is to cheat them.

clue.text: Always heard after goal or try

indicators.note: after puts the spoken piece following the word for goal

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal

indicators.note: heard says the word for always is said aloud and spelt another way

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful

explanation.surface: Someone keeps striving at a goal or a try, perhaps in rugby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goal' and 'try' suggest sport scoring, but 'try' is the definition, meaning attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: An endeavour is an earnest attempt, so a try in the sense of effort.

clue.text: A tense adult partnership, until now going nowhere

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
A is the film certificate abbreviation for adult
in cricket a stand is a partnership between two batsmen
still means up to this time, until now

explanation.surface: A strained relationship between grown-ups has stalled so far.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket STAND is the runs two batsmen add together.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at a standstill means stationary and making no progress, so going nowhere.

clue.text: What may cause danger if tossed by first to enter?

definitions.text: What may cause danger if tossed by first to enter?

indicators.note: tossed suggests the letters of danger are thrown about and rearranged
first to picks only the opening letter of enter

explanation.surface: A bomb thrown by whoever goes in first could create peril.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tossed' shuffles DANGER into GRENAD, then E from 'enter' is added; the whole clue also describes the weapon, lobbed into a room by the first soldier in.
explanation.definitionFit: A grenade is a small hand-thrown bomb, which threatens harm when thrown.

clue.text: Concede match

definitions.meaning: to admit a point is valid, accept it
to correspond or be consistent, as two accounts tally

explanation.surface: Give in during a sporting contest.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree is both to admit a claim and to correspond, as figures that tally.

clue.text: Bishop and I disarmed desperate female holding up a train?

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: desperate suggests the letters of I disarmed are in wild disorder

explanation.surface: A cleric and I overpowered a frantic woman staging a train robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding up a train' suggests a hold-up of a railway train; it means carrying the long trailing back of a bride's dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridesmaid attends the bride and may carry the long trailing fabric of her gown.

clue.text: Take back pamphlet produced by Royal Engineers

parts.note: RE is the abbreviation for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
a tract is a short pamphlet, often political or religious

explanation.surface: A leaflet issued by army engineers is withdrawn.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract a statement is to withdraw it, as one takes back words.

clue.text: Please pay in full

definitions.meaning: to give pleasure or contentment to someone
to discharge a debt or claim completely

explanation.surface: A polite request to settle the whole bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To satisfy someone is to content them; to satisfy a debt is to clear it completely.

clue.text: Almost certain to provide yield

indicators.note: almost says the word for certain falls just short, losing its last letter

parts.note: sure means certain
to render a service is to provide it

explanation.surface: Something nearly guaranteed to produce a good return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yield' looks like a harvest or return; it is the verb meaning give in.
explanation.definitionFit: To surrender is to give up to an opponent, which is to yield.

clue.text: Titled lady expected endless game

indicators.note: endless says the word for expected loses its last letter

parts.note: a train that is due is expected
chess is a board game

explanation.surface: A noblewoman anticipated a game that never finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A duchess holds a noble title, the wife of a duke or a peeress in her own right.

clue.text: Like some bacon, variable in quality

definitions.meaning: having alternating strips of fat and lean meat
uneven, good in some patches and poor in others

explanation.surface: Breakfast rashers that are inconsistent.
explanation.definitionFit: Streaky bacon has bands of fat; a streaky performance is patchy and erratic.

clue.text: Intimidate a Parisian with bottle

parts.note: a Parisian would say un, French for a
bottle is British slang for courage or nerve

explanation.surface: Threatening a Frenchman while wielding a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottle' looks like a weapon; in British slang it means courage.
explanation.definitionFit: To unnerve someone is to make them lose courage, which is to frighten or daunt them.

clue.text: Lots devoured by plump teenager

indicators.note: devoured by says the answer lies swallowed up inside the following words

explanation.surface: Plenty of food eaten by an overweight adolescent.
explanation.definitionFit: Umpteen is an informal word for a large but unspecified number, so many.

clue.text: On which notes may be written for workforce

definitions.text: On which notes may be written
definitions.meaning: the five ruled lines on which music is written

explanation.surface: A place to jot memos for the employees.
explanation.definitionFit: A staff is the set of lines carrying musical notation, and also an organisation's personnel.

clue.text: A British book on Old Testament religious leader

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the first pieces above the last

explanation.surface: A British book on the Old Testament written by a churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbot is the head of an abbey of monks, a religious leader.

clue.text: Witty response from Republican that is passed round office

indicators.note: passed round says the abbreviation goes around the word for office

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of Latin id est, meaning that is
a post is a job or office

explanation.surface: A clever comeback from a politician is circulated through the workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick, clever retort, a sharp reply in conversation.

clue.text: Rod's large cutting tool

indicators.note: cutting says the letter for large slices into the tool's name

parts.note: an axe is a chopping tool
L is the clothing abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A man called Rod owns a big chopping implement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rod' looks like a man's name; it is a bar or shaft.
explanation.definitionFit: An axle is the bar or shaft on which wheels turn, a kind of rod.

clue.text: Artist imprisoned by a bitter travelling judge

indicators.note: imprisoned by says the artist is locked inside the rearranged letters
travelling suggests the letters of a bitter are on the move into a new order

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A painter jailed by a resentful judge on circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' turns A BITTER into ARBITTE, and 'imprisoned by' puts RA inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To arbitrate is to settle a dispute impartially, as a judge does when ruling.

clue.text: Find expression? Only part of it in list

indicators.note: Only part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A puzzle about finding a phrase, partly within a catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'it in list' is wrong: 'it' points back to 'Find expression', 'in' is a link, and only 'list' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An index is an alphabetical list of topics at the back of a book.

clue.text: Information: a small amount brought back

indicators.note: brought back says these letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: a tad is a tiny amount

explanation.surface: A little information is returned.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are facts and figures collected for reference, that is, information.

clue.text: Year in orchestra — great, on the whole

indicators.note: in says the letter for year sits inside the word for orchestra

parts.note: a band is a group of musicians, an orchestra
large means great in size

explanation.surface: A musician's year with a superb orchestra, taken overall.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means generally or mostly, considering everything together.
